'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Lagos high-rise collapse]]
**At least 15 people are killed and several others are trapped when a [[high-rise building]] under construction in [[Ikoyi]], [[Lagos]], [[Nigeria]], [[structural integrity and failure|collapses]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-59125228 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on The Walt Disney Company]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Shanghai]]
*****[[Shanghai Disney Resort]] suspends entry into [[Shanghai Disneyland]] and [[Disneytown]] and asks 33,863 visitors to take a [[nucleic acid]] test upon exiting, and another test after 24 hours, after a visitor from [[Hangzhou]] tested positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/shanghai-disneyland-lockdown-officials-test-30000-visitors-rcna4226 (NBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
****The [[Indonesia]]n [[National Agency of Drug and Food Control of Indonesia|Drug and Food Control Agency]] issues an emergency use authorization for the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] vaccine for children between the ages of 6 and 11 years. [https://voi.id/en/news/99817/bpom-allows-children-6-12-years-old-to-be-injected-with-sinovac-vaccines (VOI)]
****Indonesia becomes the first country in the world to approve the protein-based [[Novavax COVID-19 vaccine]], which will be manufactured by the [[Serum Institute of India]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/01/health/novavax-vaccine-indonesia.html (''The New York Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] reopens its borders to vaccinated international travellers for the first time since March 2020, where they must have received two doses of any [[World Health Organization|WHO]]-approved [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], a booster dose within the past six months, or only one dose if they have recovered from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.laprensalatina.com/israel-reopens-borders-to-vaccinated-visitors-for-1st-time-since-march-2020/ (''La Prensa Latina'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] lifts its 10,000 spectator attendance limit for large-scale events in 27 [[Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]]s and allow events across the country to have 5,000 spectators or 50% venue capacity in order to restore social and economic activities amid decline of COVID-19 cases. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/11/d9dc44a41d6a-japan-eases-limits-on-attendance-at-large-events-as-virus-cases-fall.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] begins to implement a "Living with COVID-19" campaign with easing of movement restrictions and lifting operating hour restrictions for businesses as well as requiring proof of [[COVID-19 vaccination in South Korea|vaccination]] or a negative [[COVID-19 test]] from the previous 48 hours in order to enter high-risk venues. This comes as 75% of the South Korean population has been fully vaccinated. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/south-korea-covid19-ease-curb-vaccine-passport-2282771 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Thailand]] reopens its international borders for the first time in 18 months to [[COVID-19 vaccine|fully vaccinated]] travellers from 60 countries, where they are allowed to enter the country without quarantining, despite only 42% of the country's population being [[COVID-19 vaccination in Thailand|fully vaccinated]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-59115395 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports a record 5,449 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 747,595. [https://greekreporter.com/2021/11/01/record-high-coronavirus-cases-greece/ (Greek Reporter)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****The Ukrainian capital [[Kyiv]] begins to require [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic|vaccine certificate]]s or negative [[COVID-19 testing|test]] results in order to enter restaurants, cafés, gyms, entertainment facilities and shopping malls as well as to use public transportation in an attempt to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/new-covid-19-restrictions-force-ukraines-capital-amid-spike-cases-2021-11-01/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[Australia]] completely reopens its international borders to [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|fully vaccinated]] citizens who are currently overseas. In the past, returning citizens were staggered through arrival caps and were required to pay for two weeks of [[quarantine]]. This will also allow fully-vaccinated [[Australians]] to leave and return to the country without an exemption. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/nov/01/hugs-and-tears-as-families-reunite-at-sydney-airport-after-australias-international-border-reopens (''The Guardian'')]
***Australia fully reopens its [[maritime border]] with [[New Zealand]] for fully vaccinated travelers, who will be able to visit Australia without needing an exemption or quarantine. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/oct/31/new-zealand-australia-quarantine-free-travel-coronavirus (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 46 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.kiro7.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-46-million-death-toll-surpasses-746000/MN7WMAK6H5BKVAKTBVUIRMJLVA/ (KIRO-TV)]
**The worldwide [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death toll]] from the COVID-19 [[pandemic]] surpasses five million. The actual death toll is suspected to be higher as some countries may not have reported all deaths. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/1/covid-19s-global-death-toll-tops-5-million-in-under-2-years (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Jersey dispute]], [[France–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] announces that [[Government of France|his government]] will postpone the imposition of "tighter controls" on British imports initially scheduled for Tuesday midnight as negotiations between France, the UK, and the [[European Commission]] over the rights of French fishermen to [[Commercial fishing|fish]] in [[Jersey]]'s [[territorial waters]] continue. [https://www.expatica.com/fr/uncategorized/frances-macron-puts-midnight-deadline-over-fish-row-on-hold-306882/ (AFP via Expatica)]
*[[Algeria-Morocco relations]], [[Spain–Algeria relations]]
**[[President of Algeria|Algerian President]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] orders the termination of [[List of countries by natural gas exports|its natural gas exports]] to [[Spain]] through the [[Maghreb–Europe Gas Pipeline]] as a diplomatic measure against Morocco. The pipeline, which supplies most of [[Energy in Spain|Spain's gas]], runs through Morocco. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/10/28/spain-presses-algeria-to-guarantee-natural-gas-supply (Euronews)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Iraq]]
**A man is [[sentenced to death]] in [[Iraq]] for shooting two journalists dead while driving home in [[Basra]] in January. The court said that the man committed the [[murder]]s "with the aim of destabilising security and stability and intimidating people for [[terrorist]] purposes". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/1/iraq-court-orders-man-to-hang-for-murder-of-two-journalists (Al Jazeera)]
*[[United States federal judge]] [[Robert N. Scola Jr.]] of the [[United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida|Southern District of Florida]] dismisses seven of eight charges of [[money laundering]] against [[Colombia]]n businessman [[Alex Saab]], who is accused of moving $350 million out of [[Venezuela]] into accounts controlled in the U.S. and other countries. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/us-judge-dismisses-most-money-laundering-charges-against-maduro-ally-saab (AFP via RFI)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Nicaragua]]
**[[President of Nicaragua|President]] [[Daniel Ortega]] tightens his grip ahead of upcoming elections. [[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] announced that the [[United States]] would increase sanctions on [[Nicaraguans|Nicaraguan]] officials, accusing Ortega and his wife [[Rosario Murillo]] of staging a "sham election" in the second poorest country in [[the Americas]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/nicaraguas-ortega-seen-tightening-grip-election-that-critics-call-sham-2021-11-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Marina del Pilar Ávila Olmeda]] is sworn in as the [[Governor of Baja California]], making her the first woman to represent [[Baja California]]. [https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/latino-life/story/2021-11-01/marina-del-pilar-avila-becomes-baja-californias-first-female-governor (''San Diego Union Tribune'')]
